newsitem.title: USA: NRC says NJ Salem 2 nuke inspection to end Friday.
newsitem.headline: NRC says NJ Salem 2 nuke inspection to end Friday.

text.p: A Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) team's inspection of the Salem 2 nuclear power unit, begun two weeks ago, will end Friday, a NRC spokesman said Thursday.
"Actual onsite inspection will be completed tomorrow," the spokesman said.
The unit, in Salem, New Jersey, and adjacent unit 1, both rated at 1,106 megawatts, have been shut for more than two years after the NRC raised concerns over the unit's safety.
Following the inspection, the NRC team will evaluate improvements and conditions of Salem 2 and decide whether it is ready to return to service, the spokesman said.
NRC and Salem's operator, Newark-based Public Service Electric & Gas Co (PSE&G), are scheduled to meet June 27 to review the inspection team's findings, he said.
Asked whether NRC would grant PSE&G approval to restart Salem 2, the spokesman said, "I can't speculate right now. If everything goes as planned, they could go on line in July."
PSE&G earlier said it hopes to put Salem 2 back in service by the end of June and restore Salem 1 output in the autumn.
PSE&G is also part-owner of both Salem units. Other owners include PECO Energy Co, Delmarva Power & Light Co and Atlantic Energy Co.
